description: Grown-root EXTERIOR settlement kit — the canopy/trunk building culture the catalogue's `hist-grove-capital` and 34 other records assume (audit §4 claim `grown-root-architecture`). Pure packaging of BM&V's Bosmer tree-city (`citebosmer`) as its authors built it: the three trunk-house forms with their own balcony, door, window and liana pieces (`tronc` = trunk house, `champ` = tapered mushroom-cap house, `gland` = hanging acorn/pod house), the COMPLETE modular elevated walkway system (all 52 `passerelles/troncons` straights, climbs, turns, 45/90 curves, T/X/Y junctions, stair and end pieces) and its `kiosque` platform family (deck, side walls, railings, access ramps, fixation collar), plus the giant host trees and root base the houses are authored to hang from. Extended with HTBM Cipactli Hist roots and ramp for the ground layer, and Mud Mother Grove's Argonian lanterns, totem, bone chime, banner, woven fences, plank bridge and platforms so the settlement reads Argonian rather than Bosmer. Interiors for these dwellings come from dungeon-root-v1 (`dwelling`/`civic-hall` interior families also resolve there). NOT tropicalised: no vanilla-backed piece is present. EXCLUDED: `housetroncbalcon001` — it carries no exportable geometry (an editor marker/parent node); the usable trunk balcony is `housetroncbalcon15v001` with its `acces15d/i` approach and `endl/endr` caps. Phase 11 Part 6 sourcing gap FILLED: the kit had no stand-alone trunk COLUMN (its only trunk-like pieces are the 206 m host tree and its 44 m root flare, and every Hist mesh we hold is a whole tree with a crown), so Nine-Trunks and every future grove/ruined-trunk composition had nothing to stand up. Tropical Skyrim's Anvil giant-tree TRUNK-ONLY pieces fill it: `anvilgianttrunk` (10.5 x 10.5 x 56.4 m, 784 tris) is a bare crownless column, `anvil_palm_trunk` (17.9 x 16.6 x 33.7 m) the broader buttressed form, and `anvil_root01` (14.4 x 10.3 x 6.2 m) the authored root flare that skirts either. Same author, same set, authored to combine (they are already the flora kit's two composite jungle giants).

snapLogic.passerelles: The walkway system's own encoded grid — this is the whole reason to package it intact. `passl<len>[h<rise>]<d|i>01`: `l` = length in Bethesda units (64/128/160/256/512), `h` = the rise that segment climbs (0/32/64/128), `d`/`i` = the two authored handrail sides (droite/interieur), which must stay consistent along a run or the rail flips. `passl256h64startd01` is the authored START of a climbing run. `passturn45...` are flat/climbing 45-degree turns (`ldi`/`rdi`/`lid`/`rid` encode which side turns and which rail leads); `passcirc45r1280...` and `passcirc90r448/r576...` are true arcs at a fixed radius (1280 / 448 / 576 units) — chain only arcs of the SAME radius. `passjunct`/`passjuncx`/`passjuncy` are the T, cross and Y junctions; `passend01` terminates; `passesc128h64d01` is the stair. All pieces butt end-to-end on the deck plane with origin at the entry face, so a run is a sum of `l` values and its height a sum of `h` values.
snapLogic.kiosque: A platform node dropped into a walkway run: `kiosk01` deck, `kioskaccesd01`/`kioskaccesi01` the two approach ramps that mate to a `pass...` end, `kioskbarriered01`/`kioskbarrierei01` the railings, `kioskmurd01`/`kioskmuri01` the solid sides, `kioskfixation001` the collar that ties it to a trunk.
snapLogic.houses: Each house form is a shell plus its OWN accessory family; do not cross forms. `housetronc001` takes `housetroncbalcon*` (with `acces15d/i` approach and `endl/endr` caps), `housetroncdooret/rc01` and `housetroncwindowet/rc00x`. `housechamp001` takes the `45v` balcony family, the `acceslat*` lateral accesses, `finl/finr` end caps and `housechampwindow00x`. `housegland001` hangs and takes `houseglandacceslatd/i01`, its own door and `windowet/rc` set. `housechamplianess001`/`lianestronc` and `housetronc001lianess` are the authored liana drops that visually tie a house to the tree.
snapLogic.trees: `treegiant01` is the host trunk, `treegiantbranche1-7/12/13` the boughs and `treegiantbrancheleaves01b/03/04` the foliage; `treegiantrootbase01` is the root flare at the base. Houses and walkways are hand-attached to boughs — there are no snap points, the branch geometry is the guide.
snapLogic.unitScale: Bethesda units; 0.0142240 m/unit. Measured extents in settlement-root-v1.kit.json.
snapLogic.trunkColumns: Stand-alone Hist/grove trunks, for rings of trunks and ruined trunks with no dwelling built in. `anvilgianttrunk` is a crownless column measuring 10.5 m across x 56.4 m tall at scale 1; a blueprint gets the Nine-Trunks brief (3-8 m across, 15-30 m tall) with a uniform scale of about 0.35-0.5 (0.45 -> 4.7 m x 25 m). `anvil_palm_trunk` is the stouter, buttressed alternative (17.9 x 16.6 x 33.7 m; ~0.3 -> 5.4 m x 10 m, so use it where a short heavy bole is wanted). `anvil_root01` is the root flare skirt authored for both and sits at the base at the same scale. Origin is at the base, +Z up, so a trunk is placed on the ground plane with no offset. Walkways and tap lines attach the same way houses attach to `treegiant01`: by hand against the geometry, no snap points. Vet note (measured on the built kit): `anvilgianttrunk` is base-anchored, so it drops straight onto the ground plane; `anvil_palm_trunk` sits 0.38 m below its pivot and `anvil_root01` 3.63 m above its base, so both need bottom-anchoring at placement rather than a raw origin drop.
